models._description: Picking Type (+auto_batch / wave grouping / capacity config)

security.note: No own groups; reuses stock.group_stock_user for all 3 access rules (stock.picking.batch, stock.picking.to.batch, stock.add.to.wave).

behavioral_notes.observation: The batch lifecycle (draft -> in_progress -> done/cancel) is a thin orchestrator over its member stock.picking states, not an independent workflow. action_confirm propagates self.picking_ids.action_confirm() to confirm every member transfer, runs _check_company and sets state='in_progress'. action_done runs a batch-wide _sanity_check(separate_pickings=False), detaches empty 'waiting'/'assigned' pickings (removed from the batch, not cancelled), then calls button_validate() on all non-empty members with context skip_sanity_check + pickings_to_detach + batches_to_validate so per-picking validation is suppressed in favor of the single batch validation. state is itself a stored compute (_compute_state): the batch auto-flips to 'cancel' when all member pickings are cancelled and to 'done' when all non-cancelled members are done - so validating/cancelling the underlying transfers drives the batch state. This propagation and empty-picking detachment are invisible in metadata.

Wave picking splits a picking's demand at the move-line level rather than grouping whole transfers. _add_to_wave takes selected stock.move.line records: if all of a picking's lines/moves are taken it simply links the whole picking to the wave (a stock.picking.batch with is_wave=True); otherwise it copy_data-clones the picking into a new split picking, calls move._split(qty) to carve the taken quantity into a new stock.move, and reassigns those move lines - leaving the remainder on the original picking. _auto_wave (triggered from stock.move._action_assign and picking.button_validate on backorders) buckets reservable move lines by the picking type's wave_group_by_product / wave_group_by_category (limited to wave_category_ids) / wave_group_by_location (nearest parent in wave_location_ids), trying existing waves first then creating new ones. None of this product/zone splitting logic is derivable from field metadata.

user_id is the worker the batch is assigned to (tracked field). On write of user_id (or when pickings are added), stock.picking.batch.write calls self.picking_ids.assign_batch_user(vals['user_id']), which cascades the responsible user down onto every member stock.picking (writing picking.user_id) and posts a chatter message 'Assigned to ... Responsible' / 'Unassigned responsible' per picking. So assigning a batch to one operator transitively re-owns all its transfers - a cross-model side effect not visible in the schema.

stock.picking.type gains auto_batch plus batch_max_lines and batch_max_pickings capacity caps and group-by flags (partner/destination/src_loc/dest_loc for batches; product/category/location for waves). When a picking reaches 'assigned' (stock.picking.action_confirm -> _find_auto_batch, also stock.move.write / _assign_picking_post_process), the module searches for a compatible non-done batch of the same picking type/company/grouping and inserts the picking only if _is_picking_auto_mergeable passes (len(move_ids)+picking.move_ids <= batch_max_lines and len(picking_ids)+1 <= batch_max_pickings); else it pairs it with another loose compatible picking into a new batch, else creates a singleton batch - auto-confirming when batch_auto_confirm is set. A constraint (_validate_auto_batch_group_by) forces at least one group-by when auto_batch is on. This scheduler-like grouping/capacity behavior is pure code.

Two or more batch/wave transfers can be merged: action_merge validates they share operation type, is_wave flag and state (and are not done/cancel), then folds every other batch's move_line_ids and picking_ids into the first, copies the earliest-scheduled batch's user/description/scheduled_date, and unlinks the absorbed batches - returning a client notification linking the surviving batch.

1 JS file, 0 OWL components, 1 registry registration (fields:stock_picking_many2many - a Many2many widget for picking selection); no patches; bundles ['web.assets_backend', 'web.assets_tests']. The module is almost entirely server-side ORM/automation with only a thin widget addition.

it_architecture.application: stock_picking_batch (Batch & Wave Transfer add-on to the Inventory application component)
data_objects: stock.picking.type (inherited: auto_batch, batch_max_lines, batch_max_pickings, wave/batch group-by)
information_flows: side-effect: stock.picking.batch.action_confirm -> stock.picking.action_confirm on every member transfer (state -> in_progress)
side-effect: stock.picking.batch.action_done -> batch-wide _sanity_check + detach empty pickings + stock.picking.button_validate on all members (validation propagated to member pickings)
side-effect: stock.picking.batch._compute_state <- member stock.picking states (auto done/cancel)
side-effect: stock.picking.batch.write(user_id) -> stock.picking.assign_batch_user (responsible cascaded onto member pickings + chatter)
side-effect: stock.picking.action_confirm / stock.move._action_assign -> _find_auto_batch / _auto_wave (auto-grouping into batches/waves under capacity limits)
side-effect: stock.move.line._add_to_wave -> stock.move._split + stock.picking.copy_data (picking split into a wave)
upstream: stock reservation/backorders feed auto-batch and auto-wave grouping

capabilities: Group Transfers into a Batch (multi-picking batch transfer)
Wave Picking (split & group picking lines by product/category/zone)
Assign Batch to a Worker (responsible cascade)
Batch Capacity Control (max lines / max transfers)

Wave-pick: select move lines -> split pickings into a wave by product/category/location -> single optimized pick walk
Execute-batch: action_confirm (in_progress) -> pick all members together -> action_done -> button_validate all -> backorders re-batched

stock.picking.type.auto_batch + group-by flags: automatic batch grouping policy (partner/destination/source loc/dest loc)
batch_max_lines / batch_max_pickings: batch capacity limits enforced by _is_picking_auto_mergeable
_validate_auto_batch_group_by: constraint requiring >=1 group-by when auto_batch enabled
stakeholders: Warehouse Operator / Picker (res.users via stock.picking.batch.user_id, Responsible)
Inventory Manager (stock.group_stock_manager, defines batch/wave operation-type rules)
Customer (res.partner, delivery destination of grouped transfers)
metrics: stock.picking.type.count_picking_batch / count_picking_wave (dashboard counts of open batches/waves)
action_report_picking_batch (batch picking operations report / pick list)

classification.rationale: stock_picking_batch sits inside the same value-chain (Porter) logistics flow as its parent stock - warehouse fulfillment, the deliver value chain - so its value_model is 'chain': it organizes the physical pick/transfer of goods toward the customer. Unlike stock itself (a primary activity through which goods physically pass), this module is an efficiency/productivity layer on top: it does not create new stock moves in the ledger or own a transfer's state machine - it groups existing stock.picking into batches and waves, assigns them to a worker, and propagates confirm/validate. It optimizes HOW the warehouse executes picking (operator routing, fewer walks) rather than moving goods itself, so its activity_class is 'support'. APQC maps to 4.0 'Deliver Physical Products', specifically the 4.x warehousing / order-picking operations (operate warehousing, pick/stage product for shipment); apqc_odoo_map.tsv anchors 4.4.x outbound transportation and 4.4.1.4 delivery service policy (stock.picking.type) which this module configures via auto_batch / wave grouping.

standard_capabilities: manual batch transfer: group several stock.picking of one operation type into a stock.picking.batch
wave transfer: split picking lines and group them by product / product category / location into a wave
automatic batching & waving on confirmation/reservation (auto_batch + group-by rules on the operation type)
batch capacity limits (max lines / max transfers) honored during auto-grouping
responsible-user assignment cascaded to all member transfers
validate the whole batch at once (action_done -> button_validate) with batch-wide backorder handling
batch put-in-pack, label-layout printing, reception report, and a batch picking report
kanban dashboard counts of open batches/waves per operation type
typical_fits: pick-then-pack warehouses grouping many small deliveries into operator batches
wave picking by zone/product to minimize travel in a large warehouse
auto-batch by destination country / carrier-adjacent grouping for outbound
capacity-bounded batches (max N transfers or N lines per operator)
common_gaps: no built-in pick-path / route optimization sequencing within a batch (only grouping, not ordering the walk)
barcode-driven batch execution UX (lives in stock_barcode)
cluster / put-to-light or zone-to-zone handoff picking strategies
carrier / shipping-rate batching and load planning (delivery_* modules)
advanced labor / wave-release scheduling and KPIs beyond simple counts
